summary: Autosport released its annual Top 50 drivers list for 2023, with only a few NASCAR drivers included: William Byron (12th), Kyle Larson and champion Ryan Blaney. The article argues that five NASCAR drivers were snubbed: Chris Buescher, Denny Hamlin, Christopher Bell, Tyler Reddick and Ross Chastain, and it cites each driver's 2023 stats. It also notes that Supercars racers Shane van Gisbergen and Brodie Kostecki made the list.
one_line: Essentially Sports argues Chris Buescher, Denny Hamlin, Christopher Bell, Tyler Reddick and Ross Chastain were snubbed from Autosport's 2023 Top 50 drivers list.
key_facts: Autosport has published its annual Top 50 drivers list since 2002.
William Byron led the NASCAR drivers on Autosport's 2023 list with a 12th-place ranking; Kyle Larson and 2023 Cup Series champion Ryan Blaney also made it.
Chris Buescher had three wins, nine top-5s and 17 top-tens in 2023, with back-to-back wins at Richmond and Michigan, and finished 7th in the final standings.
Buescher's RFK Racing teammate Brad Keselowski, who arrived in 2022, failed to win a race in 2023.
Denny Hamlin had three wins, 14 top-fives and 19 top-10s in 2023, led 998 laps and finished 5th in the standings despite a shoulder injury during the playoffs.

Christopher Bell reached the championship race for a second straight season but retired early at Phoenix Raceway with a broken brake rotor; he had two wins, 19 top-tens and ten top-5s and finished fourth.
Bell's average starting position of 9.6 was the only one below 10, and he took poles in the first three playoff races.
Tyler Reddick won at COTA and Kansas, had two wins, ten top-5s and 16 top-10s, led 470 laps and finished sixth in the standings.
23XI Racing had two drivers in the Cup playoffs for the first time since its inception in 2023.
Ross Chastain became the first non-championship driver to win the Championship 4 race since the new playoff system began in 2014, winning at Phoenix.
Chastain had two wins (Nashville and Phoenix), ten top-5s, 14 top-tens, led 640 laps and led the standings for seven weeks.
Shane van Gisbergen won in his NASCAR debut at the inaugural Chicago Street Race and, with Brodie Kostecki, made Autosport's list.
